sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 在太空中走过七个十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星的背后是什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 上千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我在测试七张床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代冰淇淋。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联赛中最棒的队伍。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢一锅端食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝成立175周年，帮助你理解世界，过好每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，即可在 nytimes.com slash subscribe 享受特惠。

sentences.en: Hey, it's Natalie.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是娜塔莉。

sentences.en: Taking a quick second here because we here at The Daily are working on a fun little project,
sentences.zh: 在这里占用大家一点时间，因为我们《每日新闻》栏目的同仁正在做一个有趣的小项目，

sentences.en: something that we'll share later as a special bonus episode for New York Times subscribers.
sentences.zh: 稍后作为《纽约时报》订阅用户的特别福利单集分享给大家。

sentences.en: The idea is simple.
sentences.zh: 这个想法很简单。

sentences.en: We're going to be talking to our fascinating colleagues here at The New York Times about who they are and how they do their jobs.
sentences.zh: 我们将与《纽约时报》那些迷人的同事们聊聊他们是谁，以及他们是如何工作的。

sentences.en: And as a part of that project, we want to hear from you.
sentences.zh: 作为该项目的一部分，我们想听听你们的声音。

sentences.en: What's the one question you've had for our colleagues but never gotten the chance to ask?
sentences.zh: 你对我们的同事一直有什么问题，但却从未有机会问出口？

sentences.en: We started with games, and now we're going to go to The Times restaurant critics,
sentences.zh: 我们从游戏板块开始，现在将转向《时报》的美食评论员，

sentences.en: Tejal Rao and Ligaya Mishan.
sentences.zh: 特加尔·拉奥和利加亚·米尚。

sentences.en: They're both new to the job, and they've brought a lot of exciting changes.
sentences.zh: 他们俩都是刚上任，并带来了很多激动人心的变化。

sentences.en: One is in California.
sentences.zh: 一个在加利福尼亚。

sentences.en: The other one's in New York City.
sentences.zh: 另一个在纽约市。

sentences.en: They're no longer dining anonymously, and they're reviewing restaurants all over the country.
sentences.zh: 他们不再隐名埋姓地去餐厅，而是在全国各地进行餐馆点评。

sentences.en: I personally have a ton of questions for them.
sentences.zh: 我个人对他们有一大堆问题。

sentences.en: Like, how are they going to get fair service from restaurants?
sentences.zh: 比如，他们将如何从餐厅获得公正的服务？

sentences.en: How do they know they're not getting treated differently than us regular folks?
sentences.zh: 他们怎么知道自己没有受到与我们普通人不同的待遇？

sentences.en: How do they pick where to go?
sentences.zh: 他们是如何选择去哪里的？

sentences.en: And also, most importantly, what's their most controversial food take?
sentences.zh: 还有，最重要的是，他们最具争议的食物观点是什么？

sentences.en: Get us your questions, please, by leaving a message at 212-556-4000.
sentences.zh: 请拨打 212-556-4000 留方留言，把你们的问题告诉我们。

sentences.en: Again, that's 212-556-4000.
Okay, here's the show.
sentences.zh: 好了，节目开始。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Natalie Kittroweff.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的娜塔莉·基特罗夫。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: The world's biggest museum, a symbol of France, now a crime scene.
sentences.zh: 世界上最大的博物馆，法国的象征，如今成了犯罪现场。

sentences.en: Over the weekend, a group of thieves staged a remarkable heist at one of the world's most famous museuMs.
sentences.zh: 周末期间，一伙窃贼在世界上最著名的博物馆之一策划了一起惊天盗窃案。

sentences.en: Officials in Paris say the masked crooks used a basket lift and cutting tools to just break into a gallery.
sentences.zh: 巴黎官方表示，这群蒙面大盗使用了一辆升降车和切割工具强行闯入了一个展厅。

sentences.en: Stealing some of the most precious and culturally significant jewels in Europe, in the middle of Paris, in broad daylight.
sentences.zh: 在白昼之下的巴黎市中心，盗走了欧洲最珍贵、最具文化意义的一些珠宝。

sentences.en: It's like a scene from a film.
sentences.zh: 这就像电影里的场景。

sentences.en: Yeah, you could not make it up.
sentences.zh: 是啊，简直编都编不出来。

sentences.en: I thought it was a joke.
sentences.zh: 我以为是个玩笑。

sentences.en: Like, no, not possible.
sentences.zh: 就觉得，不可能，这绝对不可能。

sentences.en: As new details emerge about the brazen theft at the Louvre, the response in France has been a mix of shock, disbelief, and fascination.
sentences.zh: 随着卢浮宫大胆盗窃案的新细节不断浮出水面，法国国内的反应充满了震惊、难以置信和着迷。

sentences.en: This is the heist of the decade, you know.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是十年来最大的盗窃案。

sentences.en: It's as bad as it gets.
sentences.zh: 这简直不能再糟糕了。

sentences.en: How could the world's most visited museum be robbed with such brazen audacity?
sentences.zh: 世界上参观人数最多的博物馆怎么会遭到如此胆大妄为的抢劫？

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Catherine Porter explains how the robbery happened and why so many feel as though they may have just lost a piece of their history for good.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事凯瑟琳·波特将解释这场抢劫是如何发生的，以及为什么许多人感觉他们刚刚永远失去了历史的一部分。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, October 22nd.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月22日，星期三。

sentences.en: Catherine, hi.
sentences.zh: 凯瑟琳，你好。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 最近怎么样？

sentences.en: This is probably the only taping where I've literally been like, I need us to begin so I can ask my questions right now.
sentences.zh: 这大概是我唯一一次录音时直言不讳地说：“我需要我们立刻开始，这样我才能马上问我的问题。”

sentences.en: I mean, that's not true.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这倒也不是真的。

sentences.en: It's not the only one.
sentences.zh: 这不是唯一的一次。

sentences.en: But this is a very special episode and I need to talk to you about this story.
sentences.zh: 但这是一期非常特殊的节目，我必须跟你聊聊这个故事。

sentences.en: I have read everything about this heist and I'm not satisfied still.
sentences.zh: 关于这次盗窃案的所有报道我都读过了，但我还是不满足。

sentences.en: I am ready for you.
sentences.zh: 我随时准备着呢。

sentences.en: Okay, good.
sentences.zh: 好的，太好了。

sentences.en: Just to start, tell me exactly how a group of jewel thieves broke into the Louvre and stole these very precious iteMs.
sentences.zh: 先说说看，一伙珠宝大盗究竟是如何闯入卢浮宫并偷走这些极其珍贵的物品的？

sentences.en: Just start from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 就从头开始讲起吧。

sentences.en: Tell me exactly what happened as far as we know.
sentences.zh: 请据我们所知，一五一十地告诉我发生了什么。

sentences.en: As far as we know, this heist started at 9.30 last Sunday morning.
sentences.zh: 据我们所知，这起盗窃案始于上周日上午9点30分。

sentences.en: Typical, kind of quiet, Paris morning.
sentences.zh: 那是一个典型而又安静的巴黎早晨。

sentences.en: And what we know is this truck that had a ladder attached to it rolls up to Louvre with two motorcycles.
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的是，一辆挂着梯子的卡车带着两辆摩托车开到了卢浮宫。

sentences.en: Now, you might wonder why is there a truck with a ladder on it, but in Paris, it's a pretty common sight
sentences.zh: 现在，你可能会好奇为什么会有一辆带着梯子的卡车，但在巴黎，这是一种相当常见的景象，

sentences.en: because this is how you move your furniture in and out of your apartments because of how skinny the halls are.
sentences.zh: 因为由于走廊太窄，大家都是用这种方式把家具搬进搬出公寓的。

sentences.en: So it rolls up, parks right up against the building on the sidewalk, and two people pop out and they set out traffic pylons around the truck
sentences.zh: 所以它开了过来，直接停在人行道的建筑紧贴处，两个人跳下车，在卡车周围摆上了交通锥，

sentences.en: and they have fluorescent vests on like public workers do.
sentences.zh: 他们还穿着像公共清洁工那样的荧光背心。

sentences.en: So like anybody looking at this from the outside might think this is a completely normal scene.
sentences.zh: 所以任何从外面看到这一幕的人都可能会认为这是一个完全正常的场景。

sentences.en: Nothing to see here.
sentences.zh: 没什么好看的。

sentences.en: Nothing necessarily to see except for the two men that then went up this electric ladder to the balcony on the second floor were masked.
sentences.zh: 除了那两个随后顺着这个电动梯子爬到二楼阳台的人戴着面具之外，其实没什么特别好看的。

sentences.en: So that might have tipped you off if you were there, but to be honest, this is the quiet side of the Louvre.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你当时在那里，这或许会给你提个醒，但老实说，这是卢浮宫比较安静的一侧。

sentences.en: It's near the Seine.
sentences.zh: 它靠近塞纳河畔。

sentences.en: Not a lot of foot traffic.
sentences.zh: 行人并不多。

sentences.en: So they go up the mechanical elevator in a kind of bucket, like a cherry picker.
sentences.zh: 所以他们坐着类似高空作业车那种斗式机械升降机上去。

sentences.en: They get to this balcony onto the second floor of the Louvre, and they use what are known as angle grinders.
sentences.zh: 他们到达了卢浮宫二楼的这个阳台，并使用了所谓的角磨机。

sentences.en: Which is what exactly?
sentences.zh: 那到底是什么？

sentences.en: Kind of like electric handsaw.
sentences.zh: 有点像电动手锯。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: To saw through the window that leads into what's known as the Apollo Gallery.
sentences.zh: 用来锯开通往所谓阿波罗长廊的窗户。

sentences.en: It's this golden, long, beautiful wing of the Louvre that literally was built by Louis XIV as a model for his Hall of Mirrors.
sentences.zh: 那是卢浮宫金碧辉煌、漫长而美丽的侧翼，实际上是路易十四为他的镜厅建造的模本。

sentences.en: And it houses the royal jewels of France.
sentences.zh: 里面藏有法国的皇家珠宝。

sentences.en: Is this like a very popular part of the Louvre?
sentences.zh: 这是卢浮宫里非常热门的区域吗？

sentences.en: It certainly sounds as though it's iconic.
sentences.zh: 听上去它绝对是个标志性景点。

sentences.en: Super iconic.
sentences.zh: 超级标志性。

sentences.en: It's not as popular, obviously, as the Mona Lisa.
sentences.zh: 当然，它的热度显然比不上《蒙娜丽莎》。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: But it's pretty close.
sentences.zh: 但也差不离了。

sentences.en: You know, when you go in there, it's often quite crowded.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你走到那里时，通常挤满了人。

sentences.en: It's really opulent.
sentences.zh: 里面真的极其奢华。

sentences.en: There's paintings on the ceilings, on the walls by famous people like Delacroix.
sentences.zh: 天花板和墙壁上有德拉克罗瓦等名家的画作。

sentences.en: There are hanging tapestries.
sentences.zh: 挂着挂毯。

sentences.en: There are sculptures and these cases down the middle that hold the crown jewels.
sentences.zh: 有雕塑，还有中间摆放着皇冠珠宝的展柜。

sentences.en: The thieves break in using the saw.
sentences.zh: 窃贼用锯子强行闯入。

sentences.en: We hear from people who work in the Louvre that there was an explosion of glass.
sentences.zh: 我们从卢浮宫的工作人员那里听说，当时玻璃碎裂的声音犹如爆炸一般。

sentences.en: And there were a number of security guards inside who really quickly evacuated the room.
sentences.zh: 里面有几名保安非常迅速地疏散了房间。

sentences.en: So they didn't approach the thieves?
sentences.zh: 所以他们没有上前去阻拦小偷吗？

sentences.en: No, the protocol in the Louvre and most museums is if you are confronted with an intruder that had things that seem like they could be weapons, your priorities protect people.
sentences.zh: 没有，卢浮宫和大多数博物馆的规程是，如果你遇到看起来可能持有武器的闯入者，你的首要任务是保护人员安全。

sentences.en: So they did what they were instructed to do, what they've been trained to do.
sentences.zh: 所以他们照着被指示的那样做了，做好了他们受过的训练。

sentences.en: They got people out and very, very quickly.
sentences.zh: 他们非常、非常迅速地把人疏散了出去。

sentences.en: And how many people were there at the time?
sentences.zh: 当时有多少人在场？

sentences.en: I mean, 9.30 a.m.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，周日上午9点30分，

sentences.en: on a Sunday does not seem like the ideal time to rob the most famous museum in the world.
sentences.zh: 似乎并不是抢劫世界上最著名博物馆的理想时间。

sentences.en: Was it crowded?
sentences.zh: 当时人多拥挤吗？

sentences.en: Well, we don't know how many people were in that room.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们不知道那个房间里有多少人。

sentences.en: That's like one of the details that has not surfaced yet or been disclosed by investigators.
sentences.zh: 这是尚未浮出水面或尚未被调查人员透露的细节之一。

sentences.en: We do know that the Louvre is like the most visited museum in the world.
sentences.zh: 我们确实知道卢浮宫是世界上参观人数最多的博物馆。

sentences.en: Up to 30,000 people visit every day.
sentences.zh: 每天有多达3万人参观。

sentences.en: We've seen videos and spoken to people who were quite frantic, not knowing why they were being evacuated.
sentences.zh: 我们看过视频，也和当时惊慌失措、不知道为什么要被疏散的人交谈过。

sentences.en: Many were running to get out.
sentences.zh: 许多人夺门而逃。

sentences.en: I mean, there was huge fear at first that either there was a fire or this was a terrorist attack.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，起初人们非常恐慌，以为要么发生了火灾，要么这是一场恐怖袭击。

sentences.en: So the thieves are inside.
sentences.zh: 所以窃贼已经进去了。

sentences.en: What happens next?
sentences.zh: 接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: What we know is that they go like directly to two cases that are in the middle of the line of cases.
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的是，他们直奔位于展柜行列中间的两个展柜。

sentences.en: And they use their power saws to cut into them and break them open.
sentences.zh: 他们用电动锯切开展柜并将其强行砸开。

sentences.en: I had heard there was some video footage taken of the thieves stealing the pieces.
sentences.zh: 我听说有一些关于窃贼偷盗这些藏品的视频片段。

sentences.en: Do we know anything about how they were acting, what they were doing, their general demeanor at the time?
sentences.zh: 我们是否知道关于他们的行为、他们在做什么以及当时总体表现的任何信息？

sentences.en: Yeah, we've seen those videos.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们看过那些视频。

sentences.en: They were given, I guess, to a local French TV station.
sentences.zh: 我想它们是被交给了当地的一家法国电视台。

sentences.en: They're quite blurry, but you see clearly one of the two men wearing something over his head, like a black covering on his head.
sentences.zh: 画面相当模糊，但你可以清楚地看到其中一名男子头上戴着遮挡物，比如黑色的头套。

sentences.en: He's got his yellow vest on and he just, he looks incredibly calm.
sentences.zh: 他穿着黄色背心，看起来镇定得不可思议。

sentences.en: Like there's no franticness.
sentences.zh: 一点慌乱也没有。

sentences.en: He's just sawing away.
sentences.zh: 他就在那儿一直锯着。

sentences.en: What we have been told by the chief Paris prosecutor who is in charge of leading the investigation into this is that these are seasoned.
sentences.zh: 负责领导此次调查的巴黎首席检察官告诉我们，这些人是老手。

sentences.en: They think that they're part of a gang, they clearly knew what they were coming for.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这些人是一个团伙的一部分，并且显然是有备而来。

sentences.en: They were pretty precise and fast and they didn't seem panicked at all.
sentences.zh: 他们相当精准、迅速，而且看起来一点也不慌张。

sentences.en: But all this was, you know, fairly quick.
sentences.zh: 但所有这一切，你知道的，相当迅速。

sentences.en: Our timeline shows that they arrived outside the building at 9.30.
sentences.zh: 我们的时间线显示他们在9点30分抵达大楼外部。

sentences.en: They got up to that window on the top of the mechanical ladder.
sentences.zh: 他们顺着机械梯爬上了那扇窗户。

sentences.en: Four minutes later, they broke in and they were out within four minutes and down and gone.
sentences.zh: 四分钟后他们闯了进去，并在四分钟内得手离开、下楼并逃之夭夭。

sentences.en: So, amazing.
sentences.zh: 所以，太惊人了。

sentences.en: That's pretty faSt.
sentences.zh: 这相当快。

sentences.en: I mean, I know in terms of heists, it's not the fasteSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我知道就抢劫案而言，这算不上最快的。

sentences.en: There have many faster.
sentences.zh: 还有许多比这更快的。

sentences.en: People who study this stuff say it's not crazy fast, but it was fast enough that they escaped and they have not been found.
sentences.zh: 研究这些东西的人说这不算疯狂地快，但快到足以让他们逃脱且至今未被找到。

sentences.en: So, okay, let's talk about that escape.
sentences.zh: 那么，好吧，我们来谈谈那次逃跑。

sentences.en: I'm trying to imagine it.
sentences.zh: 我在脑海里想象着这个画面。

sentences.en: What does it actually look like?
sentences.zh: 它到底长什么样？

sentences.en: You know, they jump out the window that they came in.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们从进来的窗户跳出去。

sentences.en: They go down the same bucket, ladder to the bottom.
sentences.zh: 他们顺着原来的那个斗式梯子回到地面。

sentences.en: We understand also that they, at this point, attempt to set fire to the truck, to the bucket itself.
sentences.zh: 我们还了解到，他们在此时试图放火焚烧卡车，烧毁那个吊斗本身。

sentences.en: We don't know why.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道原因何在。

sentences.en: There's been lots of speculation they were trying to remove any kind of DNA or fingerprints, basically.
sentences.zh: 有很多猜测认为他们基本上是想消除任何种类的DNA或指纹痕迹。

sentences.en: And at this point, what we know is that some security guard or guards come chasing towards them on the ground.
sentences.zh: 在这个时候，据我们所知，地面上有一些保安追了上来。

sentences.en: They drop a couple things, including one of their security vests and the bottle that they were using to spray gas onto this cherry bin to light it on fire.
sentences.zh: 他们扔下了几样东西，包括一件保安背心，以及用来将汽油喷到高空作业车上点燃的瓶子。

sentences.en: And they jump on the back of two waiting motorcycles and speed away.
sentences.zh: 然后他们跳上在旁边接应的两辆摩托车，加速逃跑。

sentences.en: One, you know, very juicy detail is that they dropped one of the nine things they originally grabbed.
sentences.zh: 有一个，你知道的，非常吸睛的细节，那就是他们丢下了原本抢走的九件物品中的一件。

sentences.en: Right, I read that.
sentences.zh: 没错，我读到过这个。

sentences.en: It was this incredibly precious crown, an imperial crown, that was made for the last empress of France, who was married to Napoleon III.
sentences.zh: 这是一顶极其珍贵的皇冠，一顶帝国皇冠，是为法国最后一位皇后（拿破仑三世的妻子）制作的。

sentences.en: I can tell you a little bit about it.
sentences.zh: 我可以向你介绍一点关于它的情况。

sentences.en: I have been learning a ton about these type of things.
sentences.zh: 我最近恶补了大量这方面的知识。

sentences.en: You're like the world's expert in crown jewels now.
sentences.zh: 你现在就像是世界上对皇室珠宝最有研究的专家了。

sentences.en: Well, not before this, but I have become one.
sentences.zh: 好吧，在这之前不是，但我现在确实成了。

sentences.en: Hold on.
sentences.zh: 等一下。

sentences.en: So this crown had eight golden eagles on it, 1,354 regular diamonds, and then 1,136 rose-cut diamonds, as well as 56 pretty sizable emeralds.
sentences.zh: 所以这顶皇冠上有八只金鹰、1,354颗常规钻石、1,136颗玫瑰切割钻石，还有56颗相当大的祖母绿宝石。

sentences.en: Okay, so they dropped this crown, but they did manage to get eight iteMs.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们把这顶皇冠掉落了，但他们确实设法弄到了八件物品。

sentences.en: Take me through what those were.
sentences.zh: 你带我回顾一下那些都是什么吧。

sentences.en: What were some of the biggest gets?
sentences.zh: 都有哪些比较贵重的失窃品？

sentences.en: So, you know, again, my crash course in learning about royal jewelry, a lot of these items stem from either Napoleon III or Napoleon himself.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，再次强调，我这是在恶补皇室珠宝的知识，其中很多物品要么源自拿破仑三世，要么源自拿破仑本人。

sentences.en: So I'll take you through a couple.
sentences.zh: 那我带你了解其中几件。

sentences.en: There was this incredible emerald necklace and earring set that Napoleon gave to his second wife for their wedding in 1810.
sentences.zh: 有一套令人惊叹的祖母绿项链和耳环套装，是拿破仑在1810年结婚时送给他第二任妻子的。

sentences.en: So that's just one.
sentences.zh: 所以这只是其中之一。

sentences.en: Then there's this decorative bow that was worn by Empress Eugenie that has more than 2,000 diamonds.
sentences.zh: 然后是尤金妮皇后佩戴过的一个装饰性蝴蝶结，上面有两千多颗钻石。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: I saw a picture of that one.
sentences.zh: 我见过那个的照片。

sentences.en: I was, like, hard to look at.
sentences.zh: 我当时就觉得，简直没法直视。

sentences.en: It was so shiny, even just in the pictures, you know.
sentences.zh: 太耀眼了，哪怕只是在照片里，你懂的。

sentences.en: And there's, like, a pearl kind of tiara that's also incredibly jaw-dropping.
sentences.zh: 还有一种珍珠冠冕，同样让人惊掉下巴。

sentences.en: But, Natalie, one thing that points to that these thieves knew what they were doing is they didn't go for what was really the most expensive item in those cases.
sentences.zh: 但是，娜塔莉，有一个迹象表明这些小偷知道自己在做什么，那就是他们并没有去拿那些展柜里真正最昂贵的东西。

sentences.en: They went for these items, and there's lots of discussion about, you know,
sentences.zh: 他们拿了这些东西，并且有很多讨论都在说，你知道的，

sentences.en: maybe they thought these ones would be easier to break down and easier to smell and break apart and sell in small pieces.
sentences.zh: 也许他们觉得这些东西更容易拆解，更容易熔化并砸碎成小块拿去出售。

sentences.en: But, you know, among those cases is this incredible diamond that's known as the regent that was bought by the Duke of Orleans in, like,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，在这些展柜中，有一颗被称为“摄政王”的不可思议的巨钻，它是在18世纪初左右被奥尔良公爵买下的，

sentences.en: the early 1700s and was on the centerpiece of Louis XV's crown and then later was on Napoleon's sword on Louis XVI's crown.
sentences.zh: 曾是路易十五皇冠的中心饰品，后来又镶嵌在路易十六皇冠以及拿破仑的宝剑上。

sentences.en: And it's, like, the size of plum.
sentences.zh: 而且它有李子那么大。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: But lots of jewelry experts say it would be just far too easy to identify and really hard to pawn off.
sentences.zh: 但许多珠宝专家表示，这东西太容易辨认了，极难脱手。

sentences.en: So,
sentences.zh: 所以，

sentences.en: we have a sense that this is more of a commodity grab than an attempt to get beautiful heritage pieces for some kind of kooky specialist collector who wants to hold things alone in a vault.
sentences.zh: 我们觉得这更像是一场大宗商品抢劫，而不是为了给某个想要把文物独自锁在保险库里的古怪狂热收藏家去搜罗美丽的历史珍品。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so, if you're going for commodities, you're looking for things that can be quickly disassembled and sold in small pieces.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你追求的是商品价值，你就会寻找那些可以被快速拆卸并切成小块出售的东西。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: These are thieves, the idea is, who are looking to sell these things and make money, not, you know, mount them in their homes.
sentences.zh: 大家的看法是，这些小偷旨在出售这些东西并赚钱，而不是把它们挂在家里的墙上。

sentences.en: I can imagine it's a lot easier, right, to sell a single diamond than a distinctive necklace, for example.
sentences.zh: 我可以想象，卖掉一颗单一的钻石肯定比卖一条独特的项链要容易得多，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, you can't sell that distinctive necklace because it's already been traced.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你没法卖那条独特的项链，因为它已经被追踪到了。

sentences.en: You know, like, Interpol has put it on its liSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，比如国际刑警组织已经把它列入了名单。

sentences.en: You would get caught very, very quickly.
sentences.zh: 你很快就会被抓到的。

sentences.en: But the idea of what experts are telling us is that you would break it down into small pieces,
sentences.zh: 但专家告诉我们的想法是，你会把它拆解成小块，

sentences.en: maybe carve some of the larger stones into smaller stones so they're less identifiable.
sentences.zh: 也许把一些较大的石头切割成较小的石头，这样它们就不那么容易被辨认了。

sentences.en: You know, one expert says you string them into a different kind of necklace and sell it and pawn it off that way.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一位专家说你可以把它们串成另一种项链，然后以此出售并典当出去。

sentences.en: But certainly, if you try and auction anything off, people will be on the alert looking for these things.
sentences.zh: 但当然，如果你试图拍卖任何东西，人们都会保持警惕，寻找这些物品。

sentences.en: Can I ask, you know, everybody's been talking about these crown jewels as priceless.
sentences.zh: 请问，大家都一直在谈论这些无价的皇室珠宝。

sentences.en: But obviously, there is a price that you can attach to these things, right?
sentences.zh: 但显然，这些东西也是可以标上价格的，对吧？

sentences.en: Do we know what was the worth of the things they stole?
sentences.zh: 我们知道他们偷的东西值多少钱吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, we just found out.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们刚刚知道了。

sentences.en: Up until now, there's been lots of speculation about how much they might have escaped with.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，关于他们可能携走多少财物有各种各样的猜测。

sentences.en: But the head of the investigation just went on public radio literally minutes ago and said that the estimation they have is they're worth 88 million euros.
sentences.zh: 但调查负责人就在几分钟前刚刚接受公共电台采访，称他们估计这些物品价值8800万欧元。

sentences.en: Whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Which is a ton.
sentences.zh: 这可是一大笔钱。

sentences.en: But she also said this interesting thing.
sentences.zh: 但她也说了一件很有趣的事。

sentences.en: She said, look, you know, if you were to break them apart and melt them down, they'd be worth a lot less.
sentences.zh: 她说，听着，你知道的，如果你把它们拆开并熔化，它们的价值就会大打折扣。

sentences.en: In some ways, almost beseeching to the thieves, like, please don't do this.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这几乎是在恳求小偷：拜托，千万别这么做。

sentences.en: You know, you're not going to make as much money as how we read it in the office.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你们赚到的钱不会像我们在办公室里计算的那样多。

sentences.en: For what purpose, do you think?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是出于什么目的？

sentences.en: Out of a desire to keep these precious items intact?
sentences.zh: 是为了让这些珍贵的物品保持完整吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, even if they're worth 88 million euros, I think, to the country of France and the history of the country, they're worth a ton more.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，即使它们价值8800万欧元，我认为对于法国这个国家和它的历史来说，它们的价值要高得多。

sentences.en: Historically, symbolically, culturally, these things are priceless.
sentences.zh: 从历史、象征和文化的角度来看，这些东西是无价的。

sentences.en: And so I think in some ways, a lot of people have been talking about, you know, how much they'd be worth.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为在某种程度上，许多人一直在讨论它们的价值。

sentences.en: But really, the loss is more emotional for the country than I think it is financial.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，对这个国家来说，情感上的损失远大于金酸损失。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wenna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》游戏板块字谜游戏“连线”（Connections）的创作者。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基。

sentences.en: And I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我每天都创作拼字游戏（Spelling Bee）和电影社交应用（Letterboxd）。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉症的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像刚刚你听到声音的人这样的一群人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 请访问 nytimes.com/games 从今天开始游玩。

sentences.en: So I want to ask just about the reaction to some of this.
sentences.zh: 所以我想问一下各方对此事的反应。

sentences.en: If the assumption is that these thieves are going to break these things down, maybe melt down the gold, sell it for parts, make as much money as possible.
sentences.zh: 如果假设这些小偷打算把这些东西拆开，也许把黄金熔化，拆散出售，以赚取尽可能多的钱。

sentences.en: How are French people responding to that possibility?
sentences.zh: 法国人对这种可能性有何反应？

sentences.en: It is the history of this country that could be disappeared.
sentences.zh: 这个国家的历史可能会因此而消失。

sentences.en: I think the predominant reaction has been shock.
sentences.zh: 我认为最主要的反应是震惊。

sentences.en: And not that at the idea of these things being melted down per se, but just at the whole of what happened on Sunday morning.
sentences.zh: 倒不是说对这些东西被熔化本身的震惊，而是对星期天早上发生的事情的整体感到震惊。

sentences.en: The fact that these people could that easily get into the Louvre has caused, you know, a lot of different kinds of emotional reactions.
sentences.zh: 这些人竟然能如此轻易地进入卢浮宫，引发了各种各样的情感反应。

sentences.en: There's been anger.
sentences.zh: 人们感到了愤怒。

sentences.en: People are stunned.
sentences.zh: 人们惊呆了。

sentences.en: Some people are quite emotional about it.
sentences.zh: 有些人对此感到相当情绪化。

sentences.en: But the country's justice minister, he said that this is a certain sign of a failure.
sentences.zh: 但法国司法部长表示，这明确标志着一种失职。

sentences.en: We have failed.
sentences.zh: 我们失败了。

sentences.en: It has been politicized.
sentences.zh: 这已经政治化了。

sentences.en: There's been people particularly on the right wing of the spectrum blaming the government for not putting enough money into security.
sentences.zh: 特别是政治光谱右翼的人一直在指责政府没有在安保上投入足够的资金。

sentences.en: There's been questions about what is the security of the Louvre.
sentences.zh: 人们开始质疑卢浮宫的安保情况。

sentences.en: And there's just been sort of people bemoaning the fact that this could happen in the center of the city, in the most famous, most visited, most coveted,
sentences.zh: 大家只是在痛心疾首地哀叹，这种事竟然会发生在城市中心，发生在法国乃至全世界最著名、访问量最大、最令人垂涎、

sentences.en: most protected museum in France and likely the world.
sentences.zh: 防护最严密的博物馆里。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The reaction that you're describing sounds like it's one of a sense of self-questioning that's happening because of just how highly trafficked this area was.
sentences.zh: 你所描述的这种反应，听起来就像是一种自我质疑的感觉，因为这个区域的客流量实在太大了。

sentences.en: How could this possibly occur?
sentences.zh: 这怎么可能发生呢？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There's that sense and also just the sense of tragedy.
sentences.zh: 不仅有那种感觉，还有一种悲剧感。

sentences.en: This country watched the Notre Dame almost burn down and people lined the banks of the Seine with tears in their eyes, you know, many of them kneeling, watching it.
sentences.zh: 这个国家眼睁睁看着巴黎圣母院差点被大火吞噬，人们含着泪水排在塞纳河畔，你知道的，许多人跪着观看。

sentences.en: I think French people living here, they are very critical culturally.
sentences.zh: 我认为生活在这里的法国人，他们在文化上非常苛刻。

sentences.en: They're people who like to strike.
sentences.zh: 他们是喜欢罢工的人。

sentences.en: They like to complain.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢抱怨。

sentences.en: They're pretty critical.
sentences.zh: 他们相当挑剔。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: But they love their history.
sentences.zh: 但他们热爱自己的历史。

sentences.en: If you go into a French bookstore, like one out of every four books is a history book.
sentences.zh: 如果你走进一家法国书店，大约每四本书里就有一本是历史书。

sentences.en: People know their history.
sentences.zh: 人们了解自己的历史。

sentences.en: They visit the museuMs.
sentences.zh: 他们参观博物馆。

sentences.en: This is like a very important cultural place in French people's hearts.
sentences.zh: 在法国人心中，这是一个非常重要的文化圣地。

sentences.en: And I think people are appalled, shocked, and really grieving to a degree.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们感到震惊、错愕，甚至在某种程度上感到深深的悲痛。

sentences.en: The thing that's really interesting is that, you know, France doesn't actually have a huge amount of royal jewels like this because of the revolution.
sentences.zh: 真正有趣的是，你知道的，由于大革命的原因，法国实际上并没有大量这样的皇室珠宝。

sentences.en: Explain that.
sentences.zh: 请解释一下。

sentences.en: So, you know, the revolution, which ended in the beheading of the king and queen at the time, at that time, the Louvre was sacked.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，大革命以当时国王和王后被斩首告终，在那时，卢浮宫被洗劫了。

sentences.en: A lot of things were stolen, including some of the jewels.
sentences.zh: 许多物品被盗，其中包括一些珠宝。

sentences.en: But then, you know, France has a really ambivalent relationship with its royal history.
sentences.zh: 但后来，你知道的，法国对自己的皇室历史有着非常矛盾的情结。

sentences.en: It's a very proud republic.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常骄傲的共和国。

sentences.en: And during one of those republics, they decided that they were going to take what was left of the royal jewels and auction them off.
sentences.zh: 在其中一个共和国时期，他们决定将剩下的皇室珠宝拿出来拍卖。

sentences.en: And that's what they did in the late 1800s.
sentences.zh: 他们在19世纪末就是这么做的。

sentences.en: They auctioned off tons of these jewels, and incredibly, the lion's share of them were bought by an American who was the founder of Tiffany's.
sentences.zh: 他们拍卖了大量的珠宝，令人难以置信的是，其中绝大部分都被蒂芙尼的创始人——一个美国人买下了。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: So, you know, the Louvre has been spending decades now trying to get them back.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，卢浮宫现在已经花了数十年时间试图把它们买回来。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: In reading about this story, I learned that this is one of several thefts from French museums this year.
sentences.zh: 我在阅读这个故事时了解到，这是今年法国博物馆发生的数起盗窃案之一。

sentences.en: Can you tell me about some of those other episodes?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我其中其他的一些事件吗？

sentences.en: Like, what is going on?
sentences.zh: 比如说，这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Even this week, there was a small museum that was burgled twice in a row.
sentences.zh: 就在这周，有一家小博物馆连续两次遭到了入室盗窃。

sentences.en: And we were looking at, like, should we do a story on this?
sentences.zh: 我们当时还在讨论，要不要做一个关于这个的故事？

sentences.en: So, it was funny that when this happened, I was like, oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 所以很有意思的是，当这件事发生时，我在想，哦，天哪。

sentences.en: But, yeah, last month, someone went into the Natural History Museum, which is only a couple subway stops away from the Louvre,
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，就在上个月，有人闯入了自然历史博物馆，它离卢浮宫只有几个地铁站的距离，

sentences.en: and using kind of similar tools, cut into some cases and took out a bunch of molten raw gold and made off with them.
sentences.zh: 并使用类似工具切开了一些展柜，拿走了大量熔化的粗金并携款潜逃。

sentences.en: In the same month, last month, a museum down in Limoges, southwest of Paris, thieves broke into a museum and stole some ancient china.
sentences.zh: 就在同一个月，上个月，巴黎西南部的利摩日的一家博物馆遭小偷破门而入，偷走了一些古代瓷器。

sentences.en: In November of last year, thieves using bats went in during the day also to a quite famous museum not far away from where I'm sitting.
sentences.zh: 去年11月，小偷带着棒球棍在大白天闯入了我坐的地方附近的一家相当著名的博物馆。

sentences.en: So, you know, there's definitely a streak of these right now in France.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，法国目前确实存在一连串此类案件。

sentences.en: Is there an understanding that these robberies are connected in any way?
sentences.zh: 人们是否认为这些抢劫案之间有什么联系？

sentences.en: I mean, I'm just wondering, it does feel like it's out of another era that you have this string of museum robberies, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我只是觉得，发生这样一连串的博物馆抢劫案，感觉像是另一个时代的事情，你知道的，

sentences.en: and I'm wondering if the thieves either are in any way working together, even loosely, or are targeting the museums for similar reasons.
sentences.zh: 我想知道小偷是否在某种程度上（哪怕是松散地）合作，或者出于相似的原因将这些博物馆作为目标。

sentences.en: There's no indication that people are working together.
sentences.zh: 没有迹象表明这些人是一起作案。

sentences.en: Yes, this seems very old-fashioned, except for in one way.
sentences.zh: 是的，这看起来非常老派，除了有一个例外。

sentences.en: This happened in broad daylight, you know, when people were in the museum.
sentences.zh: 这发生在光天化日之下，你知道的，当时博物馆里还有人。

sentences.en: And that's pretty new.
sentences.zh: 这相当新颖。

sentences.en: There's a modern art museum here that was famously burgled in the middle of the night and a man made off with five very famous tableaus.
sentences.zh: 这里有一家现代艺术博物馆，曾因在半夜遭窃而名声大噪，一个男子盗走了五幅非常著名的画作。

sentences.en: And he did it in a classic way.
sentences.zh: 他用的是经典的手法。

sentences.en: Like, when you're thinking about the movie in your head, which here is known as Lupin, it's a very famous series.
sentences.zh: 就像你脑海中想到的电影那样，这里被称为《亚森·罗宾》（Lupin），这是一部非常著名的剧集。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: If you haven't seen it, definitely watch it.
sentences.zh: 如果你没看过，一定要看。

sentences.en: I've seen it, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我看过了，是的。

sentences.en: I feel like I'm watching it in real life right now.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我现在就像是在亲历现实生活中的剧情。

sentences.en: But, you know, like, it's secret.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，这很神秘。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And often that's at night or in some way that people don't see it happening.
sentences.zh: 通常那是在晚上，或者以某种人们看不到的方式发生。

sentences.en: This is, like, very brazen in that we do know that, you know, there's CCTV cameras all around the Louvre.
sentences.zh: 而这次非常猖獗，因为我们确实知道，你知道的，卢浮宫到处都有闭路电视摄像头。

sentences.en: There were people there even.
sentences.zh: 甚至当时现场还有其他人在。

sentences.en: So it's a little bit different.
sentences.zh: 所以情况有点不太一样。

sentences.en: And the lead investigator is talking about this being, like, incredibly organized.
sentences.zh: 首席调查员谈到这次作案时，形容它“组织极其严密”。

sentences.en: She doesn't think there was just four people.
sentences.zh: 她认为作案的不止四个人。

sentences.en: She thinks that there's many more involved in this.
sentences.zh: 她认为有更多人参与其中。

sentences.en: So we don't know anything about these four guys who broke into the Louvre, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，对于闯入卢浮宫的这四个家伙，我们现在还一无所知。

sentences.en: So, you know, it's hard to say what kind of connections.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，很难说他们有什么样的背景关联。

sentences.en: But clearly they're either copycatting or there's some ring that's sponsoring them.
sentences.zh: 但很显然，他们要么是在模仿作案，要么就是有某个团伙在背后资助。

sentences.en: Those are questions that, you know, we hope to be able to answer in the weeks to come.
sentences.zh: 这些都是我们希望在未来几周内能够解答的问题。

sentences.en: What are the next steps in the investigation?
sentences.zh: 接下来的调查步骤有哪些？

sentences.en: Like, what are the investigators telling you about the manhunt for these guys, about their investigative strategies?
sentences.zh: 比如，调查人员向你透露了哪些关于追捕这些嫌疑人的搜捕行动以及他们的调查策略？

sentences.en: Do we know how they're going about trying to catch them?
sentences.zh: 我们知道他们正打算如何抓捕这些人吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不知道。

sentences.en: What we do know is that there were 60 police investigators on the case.
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的是，有60名警察调查员负责此案。

sentences.en: Now we know it's up to 100.
sentences.zh: 现在我们知道人数已经增加到了100人。

sentences.en: We know that they've been using DNA methods, fingerprinting.
sentences.zh: 我们知道他们一直在使用DNA检测方法和指纹识别。

sentences.en: They've been using surveillance cameras.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在调取监控摄像头。

sentences.en: We know that the truck was left behind.
sentences.zh: 我们知道那辆卡车被遗弃了。

sentences.en: Yeah, they didn't manage to burn it.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们没能把它烧毁。

sentences.en: They didn't manage to burn it.
sentences.zh: 他们没能把它烧毁。

sentences.en: We know that they had just recently basically stolen it.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这辆车基本上是他们不久前刚偷来的。

sentences.en: And so investigators are speaking to the person they stole it from.
sentences.zh: 所以调查人员正在与车主进行谈话。

sentences.en: But that's the gist of what we've been told by investigators.
sentences.zh: 但这就是调查人员告诉我们的全部核心内容了。

sentences.en: They are being incredibly tight-lipped about it at this point.
sentences.zh: 目前他们对此事守口如瓶。

sentences.en: I think they will speak more once and if they find them.
sentences.zh: 我想一旦他们找到这些人，或者如果找到了，他们会透露更多信息。

sentences.en: But there's a real feeling that there's a race against time to try and get them before these precious jewels are broken apart and secreted away.
sentences.zh: 但大家普遍有一种感觉，这是一场与时间的赛跑，必须在这些珍贵的珠宝被拆解并藏匿起来之前把它们找回。

sentences.en: My final question for you, Catherine, is do you think it's possible, and it sounds like it might be, that these thieves actually pulled this off?
sentences.zh: 我的最后一个问题留给你，凯瑟琳，你认为这些小偷真的能把这票干成吗？听起来好像真有可能？

sentences.en: Like, that they could get away with it?
sentences.zh: 也就是说，他们真的能逍遥法外吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I think it's possible that we will never see those jewels again.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，我认为我们可能再也见不到那些珠宝了。

sentences.en: But I think France has a pretty good record of capturing some of these people.
sentences.zh: 但我认为法国在抓捕此类犯罪分子方面有着相当不错的记录。

sentences.en: In fact, the person who is said to have broken into the Natural History Museum was just charged today.
sentences.zh: 事实上，那个据说闯入自然历史博物馆的人今天刚被起诉。

sentences.en: She was captured in Barcelona.
sentences.zh: 她在巴塞罗那被抓获了。

sentences.en: I think given the amount of cameras and evidence that the cops have, that they will be able to trace who these men were.
sentences.zh: 我认为鉴于警察掌握的大量摄像头画面和证据，他们将能够顺藤摸瓜查出这些人的身份。

sentences.en: If someone tries to sell, you know, that beautiful diamond bow that we were talking about earlier, then no doubt they'll get caught and it will be returned.
sentences.zh: 如果有人试图出售我们刚才谈到的那件漂亮的钻石蝴蝶结，那么毫无疑问他们会被抓获，珠宝也会被归还。

sentences.en: And that is the best case scenario.
sentences.zh: 那是最好的情况。

sentences.en: But if they take each of those thousand plus diamonds off and make something entirely different out of it, maybe a tiara, I don't know, an anklet,
sentences.zh: 但如果他们把那一千多颗钻石一颗颗拆下来，做成完全不同的东西，比如一个头饰，我不知道，或者一个脚链，

sentences.en: a bracelet for a very rich person, then who would notice at first?
sentences.zh: 一个给某个超级富豪戴的手链，那谁一开始会注意到呢？

sentences.en: You would need to be an expert to be able to trace those diamonds to that bow.
sentences.zh: 你必须得是专家，才能顺着这些钻石查到那个蝴蝶结上。

sentences.en: So it seems much less likely, in this case, that these beautiful pieces of French heritage will make their way back.
sentences.zh: 所以在这个案子里，这些法国文化的瑰宝还能找回来的可能性似乎要小得多。

sentences.en: Catherine, thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 凯瑟琳，非常感谢。

sentences.en: You're welcome, Natalie.
sentences.zh: 不客气，娜塔莉。

sentences.en: It was such a pleasure to be talking to you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能和你交谈。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: We are one week into President Trump's historic peace plan in the Middle East, and things are going, frankly, better than I expected that they were.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统历史性的中东和平计划已经实施一周了，坦率地说，事情的进展比我预期的要好。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, Vice President J.D.
sentences.zh: 周二，副总统J·D·

sentences.en: Vance traveled to Israel as the U.S.
sentences.zh: 万斯前往以色列，因为美国

sentences.en: seeks to shore up the fragile ceasefire deal in Gaza, which has come under strain with repeated flare-ups of violence in recent days.
sentences.zh: 正试图巩固加沙脆弱的停火协议，该协议近几天因屡次爆发暴力冲突而承受着压力。

sentences.en: Vance didn't give a deadline for Hamas to disarm, a key part of that truce agreement.
sentences.zh: 万斯并未给哈马斯解除武装设定最后期限，而这是停火协议的关键部分。

sentences.en: And he also didn't specify how officials would make sure the group agrees to do so.
sentences.zh: 他也没有具体说明官员们将如何确保该组织同意这样做。

sentences.en: We've got a lot of work left to do.
sentences.zh: 我们还有大量的工作要做。

sentences.en: This is going to take a very, very long time.
sentences.zh: 这将会花费非常、非常长的时间。

sentences.en: The vice president did express optimism that the deal would hold, but said the process of securing long-term peace would take time.
sentences.zh: 副总统确实对协议能够维持表示了乐观，但也表示实现长期和平的过程需要时间。

sentences.en: And a White House official said on Tuesday that Trump had no plans to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin in the immediate future,
sentences.zh: 一位白宫官员周二表示，特朗普目前没有计划在近期与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京会面，

sentences.en: a pivot after Trump had suggested last week that he would meet with a Russian leader soon to discuss an end to the war in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 这与特朗普上周暗示他将很快与俄罗斯领导人会面以讨论结束乌克兰战争的说法有所转变。

sentences.en: Speaking to reporters, Trump said he wanted to avoid a, quote, wasted meeting with Putin.
sentences.zh: 特朗普在对记者讲话时表示，他希望避免与普京进行一场“浪费时间的会面”。

sentences.en: White House Press Secretary Caroline Levitt said that after Trump had a call with Putin last week, the Russian leader had committed to sitting down with him.
sentences.zh: 白宫新闻秘书卡罗琳·莱维特表示，在特朗普上周与普京通电话后，这位俄罗斯领导人已承诺与他坐下来会谈。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Shannon Lynn and Caitlin O'Keefe.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由香农·林恩和凯特琳·奥基夫制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Brendan Klinkenberg.
sentences.zh: 由布伦丹·克林肯伯格剪辑。

sentences.en: Fact-checked by Susan Lee.
sentences.zh: 苏珊·李进行事实核查。

sentences.en: Contains music by Dan Powell, Pat McCusker, and Marion Lozano.
sentences.zh: 包含丹·鲍威尔、帕特·麦卡斯克和马里昂·洛扎诺的音乐。

sentences.en: And was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由克里斯·伍德担任音频工程。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日简报》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Natalie Kittroweth.
sentences.zh: 我是娜塔莉·基特罗维斯。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《电线cutter秀》节目中，我们正为假日期间招待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让你的客人们宾至如归的小窍门。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是那种对光线极度敏感、需要完全黑暗才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们会不会为了睡觉而喝到断片。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们睡觉时需要什么样的光线环境？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物禁忌吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们习惯喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点钟起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 请在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何平台上收听《电线cutter秀》。
